only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane lipid organisation and the trafficking and signalling events built on it. Its clearest core is the aminophospholipid flippase machinery: ATP11B, a P4-ATPase, must partner with the accessory subunit TMEM30A (CDC50A) to fold, reach the plasma membrane and translocate phosphatidylserine to the cytosolic leaflet, which keeps this lipid hidden until apoptosis or platelet activation exposes it.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on membrane traffic through the Golgi and the machinery that buds, tethers and fuses transport vesicles, the route by which secretory and lysosomal cargo reaches its destination. Its outputs are secretion, receptor recycling and delivery of hydrolases such as cathepsin D to lysosomes; when it falters, cargo is mislocalised and organelle identity degrades.

[untitled BTM module] Granulocyte maturation in the bone marrow, and the antimicrobial cargo that neutrophils acquire as they mature, is the theme here. Promyelocytes and myelocytes load their granules with proteins that will later be deployed against bacteria: a lipopolysaccharide-binding bactericidal protein of the BPI family, the adipokine-like secreted factor resistin, prokineticin 2, the soluble pattern-recognition molecule pentraxin 3, and a haematopoietic growth factor of the CLEC11A type that supports progenitor expansion.

[untitled BTM module] These genes mark the antimicrobial granule programme of neutrophils, the arsenal that granulocytes build during maturation in bone marrow and deploy against bacteria and fungi at sites of infection. BPI binds and permeabilises Gram-negative outer membranes through its affinity for lipopolysaccharide, lipocalin 2 sequesters bacterial siderophores to starve microbes of iron, and olfactomedin 4 defines a distinct subset of neutrophil specific granules; CEACAM8 is a surface glycoprotein used routinely to identify granulocytes and their precursors.

members: [untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is chromatin-based control of gene expression coupled to ubiquitin-dependent protein regulation. Polycomb components BMI1 and EED, the histone chaperone ANP32E, the chromatin remodeller SMARCA5 and the histone-binding MORF4L2 together repress or reposition nucleosomes at developmental and proliferation genes, keeping stem and progenitor identity stable and restraining tumour suppressor loci such as the CDKN2A region.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping brings together proteins that have in common little more than a shared place in interaction screens, yet several of them converge on mitotic and genome-maintenance functions. SSNA1 is a microtubule-associated protein that promotes filament branching and localises to centrosomes and the midbody, and RASSF7 is likewise a centrosomal Ras-association domain protein required for orderly spindle formation and mitotic entry.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on the housekeeping machinery that keeps mitochondria energetically competent while proteins and metabolites are turned over. Two accessory subunits of respiratory complex I sit alongside the mitochondrial translation elongation factor TUFM, which delivers aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitoribosome and so supplies the organelle-encoded core of the respiratory chain; PRELID1 participates in phospholipid transfer between mitochondrial membranes, and TMEM160 is an inner-membrane protein.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the regulation of gene expression at the steps between transcription and protein turnover. Cyclin T2 partners CDK9 in the elongation kinase that releases paused RNA polymerase II, while cyclin C works within the Mediator kinase module that gates promoter engagement, and ARID4A and SP3 act on chromatin and promoter DNA to set which genes are read.
